newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegetable oil prices seen holding firm.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegetable oil prices seen holding firm.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil prices are expected to remain firm this week in line with a stronger international market, dealers said on Saturday.
"Vegoil prices can slightly gain in local market as rates of the commodity is up abroad on an increased demand from India and China," dealer Saulat Khan said.
"Pakistan is also looking forward to purchase up to 12,000 tonnes of vegoil and probably will be out in the market this week," he said.
Vegoil stocks rose to 149,000 tonnes last week from 129,000 tonnes the previous week on fresh arrivals.
Dealers said RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks rose to 120,000 tonnes last week from 105,000 a week earlier. Soyoil and sunflower oil stocks went up to 23,000 tonnes from 18,000.

The state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan (GCP) has booked 9,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil by September 7. It is still awaiting 6,000 tonnes of palm oil and 3,000 tonnes of olein due to have been shipped by August 10.
One dealer said the Courage was discharging 12,500 tonnes of palm oil at Karachi, while vessels with a total of 58,000 tonnes of vegoil for Pakistan were at the outer anchorage.
He said the Bunga Tanjung, with 20,000 tonnes of palm oil, is expected to arrive at Karachi on August 29, and the Tiblsi, with 15,000 tonnes of soyoil, on September 5.
The Strength was loading 25,000 tonnes of palm oil at a Malaysian port, while the Wawasan Murni and the Antea are expected to load Malaysian vegoil in August and September respectively.
